0|4d82a1debbffec129cc387aafa8f40b7bbab3297|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"lockdep: fix oops in processing workqueue
Under memory load
process_one_work() has been seen to oops in __lock_acquire()
on a 0xffffffff00000000 pointer in the lockdep_map's class_cache[].
Because it's permissible to free a work_struct from its callout function
the map used is an onstack copy of the map given in the work_struct: and
that copy is made without any locking.
Surprisingly
column2: gcc (4.5.1 in Hugh's case) uses ""rep movsl"" rather than

column1: rep movsq"" for that structure copy: which might race with a workqueue
user's wait_on_work() doing lock_map_acquire() on the source of the
copy
column2: putting a pointer into the class_cache[]

column1: the top half of that pointer to be copied to the destination map.
Boom when process_one_work() subsequently does lock_map_acquire()
on its onstack copy of the lockdep_map.
Fix this
column2: and a similar instance in call_timer_fn()

column1: lockdep_copy_map() function which additionally NULLs the class_cache[].
Note: this oops was actually seen on 3.4-next
does the racing lock_map_acquire(); but Tejun points out that 3.4 and
earlier are already vulnerable to the same through wait_on_work().
* Patch orginally from Peter.  Hugh modified it a bit and wrote the
description.
